verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֗ן שְׁנַ֥ת עֶשְׂרִ֛ים לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥סְתְּא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יַ֣יִן לְפָנָ֑יו וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶת־ הַיַּ֙יִן֙ וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹא־ הָיִ֥יתִי רַ֖ע לְפָנָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî bə·ḥō·ḏeš nî·sān šə·naṯ ‘eś·rîm lə·’ar·taḥ·šast ham·me·leḵ ya·yin lə·p̄ā·nāw wā·’eś·śā ’eṯ- hay·ya·yin wā·’et·tə·nāh lam·me·leḵ wə·lō- hā·yî·ṯî ra‘ lə·p̄ā·nāw
verses.literal: Now in the month of Nisan in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes when wine was set before him I took the wine and gave it to the king I had never been sad in his presence
verses.literalPt: No mês de nizã, no vigésimo ano do rei Artaxerxes, como o vinho estivesse posto diante dele, eu o tomei e o ministrei ao rei. Ora, eu não tinha estado dantes triste na sua presença.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מַדּ֣וּעַ׀ פָּנֶ֣יךָ רָעִ֗ים וְאַתָּה֙ אֵֽינְךָ֣ חוֹלֶ֔ה אֵ֣ין זֶ֔ה כִּי־ אִ֖ם רֹ֣עַֽ לֵ֑ב וָאִירָ֖א הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lî ham·me·leḵ mad·dū·a‘ pā·ne·ḵā rā·‘îm wə·’at·tāh ’ê·nə·ḵā ḥō·w·leh ’ên zeh kî- ’im rō·a‘ lêḇ wā·’î·rā har·bêh mə·’ōḏ
verses.literal: so the king said to me Why is your face sad though you are not ill This could only be . . . . . . sadness of the heart I was overwhelmed with fear . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: O rei me disse: Por que está triste o teu rosto, visto que não estás doente? Isso não é outra coisa senão tristeza de coração. Então, foi em extremo grande o meu medo.

verses.original: וָאֹמַ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְעוֹלָ֣ם יִחְיֶ֑ה מַדּ֜וּעַ לֹא־ יֵרְע֣וּ פָנַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָעִ֜יר בֵּית־ קִבְר֤וֹת אֲבֹתַי֙ חֲרֵבָ֔ה וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ אֻכְּל֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃ס
verses.transliteration: wā·’ō·mar lam·me·leḵ ham·me·leḵ lə·‘ō·w·lām yiḥ·yeh mad·dū·a‘ lō- yê·rə·‘ū p̄ā·nay ’ă·šer hā·‘îr bêṯ- qiḇ·rō·wṯ ’ă·ḇō·ṯay ḥă·rê·ḇāh ū·šə·‘ā·re·hā ’uk·kə·lū ḇā·’êš
verses.literal: and replied to the king May the king live forever . . . Why should I not be sad . . . when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins and its gates have been destroyed by fire
verses.literalPt: Eu disse ao rei: Viva o rei para sempre! Porque não há de estar triste o meu rosto, quando a cidade, lugar dos sepulcros de meus pais, está deserta, e as suas portas consumidas do fogo?

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לִי֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַל־ מַה־ זֶּ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ וָֽאֶתְפַּלֵּ֔ל אֶל־ אֱלֹהֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lî ham·me·leḵ ‘al- mah- zeh ’at·tāh mə·ḇaq·qêš wā·’eṯ·pal·lêl ’el- ’ĕ·lō·hê haš·šā·mā·yim
verses.literal: What . . . is your request replied the king . . . So I prayed to the God of heaven
verses.literalPt: Perguntou-me o rei: Que me pedes tu? Orei ao Deus do céu.

verses.original: וָאֹמַ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב וְאִם־ יִיטַ֥ב עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר תִּשְׁלָחֵ֣נִי אֶל־ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־ עִ֛יר קִבְר֥וֹת אֲבֹתַ֖י וְאֶבְנֶֽנָּה׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ō·mar lam·me·leḵ ’im- ‘al- ham·me·leḵ ṭō·wḇ wə·’im- yî·ṭaḇ ‘aḇ·də·ḵā lə·p̄ā·ne·ḵā ’ă·šer tiš·lā·ḥê·nî ’el- yə·hū·ḏāh ’el- ‘îr qiḇ·rō·wṯ ’ă·ḇō·ṯay wə·’eḇ·nen·nāh
verses.literal: and answered the king If it pleases the king and if your servant has found favor in your sight I ask that you send me to Judah to the city where my fathers are buried so that I may rebuild it
verses.literalPt: Eu disse ao rei: Se for do agrado do rei, e se o teu servo tiver achado graça diante de ti, peço-te que me envies a Judá, à cidade dos sepulcros de meus pais, para que eu a reedifique.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וְהַשֵּׁגַ֣ל׀ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת אֶצְל֗וֹ עַד־ מָתַ֛י יִהְיֶ֥ה מַֽהֲלָכֲךָ֖ וּמָתַ֣י תָּשׁ֑וּב וַיִּיטַ֤ב לִפְנֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֔נִי וָֽאֶתְּנָ֥ה ל֖וֹ זְמָֽן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lî ham·me·leḵ wə·haš·šê·ḡal yō·wō·še·ḇeṯ ’eṣ·lōw ‘aḏ- mā·ṯay yih·yeh ma·hă·lā·ḵă·ḵā ū·mā·ṯay tā·šūḇ way·yî·ṭaḇ lip̄·nê- ham·me·leḵ way·yiš·lā·ḥê·nî wā·’et·tə·nāh lōw zə·mān
verses.literal: Then the king with the queen seated beside him asked me How long . . . will your journey take and when will you return So it pleased . . . the king to send me and I set a time
verses.literalPt: O rei disse-me (estando a rainha também sentada junto a ele): Que tempo durará a tua viagem? Quando voltarás? Aprouve ao rei enviar-me; e eu lhe apontei um prazo.

verses.original: וָאוֹמַר֮ לַמֶּלֶךְ֒ אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב אִגְּרוֹת֙ יִתְּנוּ־ לִ֔י עַֽל־ פַּחֲו֖וֹת עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר אֲשֶׁר֙ יַעֲבִיר֔וּנִי עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־ אָב֖וֹא אֶל־ יְהוּדָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ō·w·mar lam·me·leḵ ’im- ‘al- ham·me·leḵ ṭō·wḇ ’ig·gə·rō·wṯ yit·tə·nū- lî ‘al- pa·ḥă·wō·wṯ ‘ê·ḇer han·nā·hār ’ă·šer ya·‘ă·ḇî·rū·nî ‘aḏ ’ă·šer- ’ā·ḇō·w ’el- yə·hū·ḏāh
verses.literal: I also said to him If it pleases the king may letters be given to me for the governors west of the Euphrates so that they will grant me safe passage until I reach . . . Judah
verses.literalPt: Disse mais eu ao rei: Se for do agrado do rei, deem-se-me cartas para os governadores além do rio, para que me permitam passar até chegar a Judá;

verses.original: וְאִגֶּ֡רֶת אֶל־ אָסָף֩ שֹׁמֵ֨ר הַפַּרְדֵּ֜ס אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתֶּן־ לִ֣י עֵצִ֡ים לְ֠קָרוֹת אֶת־ שַׁעֲרֵ֨י הַבִּירָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־ לַבַּ֙יִת֙ וּלְחוֹמַ֣ת הָעִ֔יר וְלַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר־ אָב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּתֶּן־ לִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּיַד־ אֱלֹהַ֖י הַטּוֹבָ֥ה עָלָֽי׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’ig·ge·reṯ ’el- ’ā·sāp̄ šō·mêr hap·par·dês ’ă·šer lam·me·leḵ ’ă·šer yit·ten- lî ‘ê·ṣîm lə·qā·rō·wṯ ’eṯ- ša·‘ă·rê hab·bî·rāh ’ă·šer- lab·ba·yiṯ ū·lə·ḥō·w·maṯ hā·‘îr wə·lab·ba·yiṯ ’ă·šer- ’ā·ḇō·w ’ê·lāw way·yit·ten- lî ham·me·leḵ kə·yaḏ- ’ĕ·lō·hay haṭ·ṭō·w·ḇāh ‘ā·lāy
verses.literal: And may I have a letter to Asaph keeper of the king’s . . . forest so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel to the temple for the city wall and for the house I will occupy . . . And because the gracious hand of my God was upon me the king granted my requests
verses.literalPt: como também uma carta para Asafe, guarda do bosque do rei, a fim de que ele me dê madeiras para fazer vigas para as portas do castelo que pertence à casa, para os muros da cidade e para a casa em que eu entrar. O rei deu-mas, segundo a boa mão do meu Deus sobre mim.

verses.original: וָֽאָב֗וֹא אֶֽל־ פַּֽחֲווֹת֙ עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֔ר וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אִגְּר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח עִמִּי֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׂ֥רֵי חַ֖יִל וּפָרָשִֽׁים׃פ
verses.transliteration: wā·’ā·ḇō·w ’el- pa·ḥă·wō·wṯ ‘ê·ḇer han·nā·hār wā·’et·tə·nāh lā·hem ’êṯ ’ig·gə·rō·wṯ ham·me·leḵ way·yiš·laḥ ‘im·mî ham·me·leḵ śā·rê ḥa·yil ū·p̄ā·rā·šîm
verses.literal: Then I went to the governors west of the Euphrates and gave them the king’s letters The king had also sent army officers and cavalry with me
verses.literalPt: Fui ter com os governadores além do rio, e lhes entreguei as cartas do rei. Ora, o rei tinha enviado comigo capitães do exército e cavaleiros.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע סַנְבַלַּ֣ט הַחֹרֹנִ֗י וְטֽוֹבִיָּה֙ הָעֶ֣בֶד הָֽעַמֹּנִ֔י וַיֵּ֥רַע לָהֶ֖ם רָעָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א אָדָ֔ם לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ טוֹבָ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·ma‘ san·ḇal·laṭ ha·ḥō·rō·nî wə·ṭō·w·ḇî·yāh hā·‘e·ḇeḏ hā·‘am·mō·nî way·yê·ra‘ lā·hem rā·‘āh ḡə·ḏō·lāh ’ă·šer- bā ’ā·ḏām lə·ḇaq·qêš ṭō·w·ḇāh liḇ·nê yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this they were deeply disturbed . . . . . . that someone had come to seek the well-being of the Israelites
verses.literalPt: O que, tendo ouvido, Sambalá, horonita, e o servo Tobias, amonita, ficaram em extremo agastados por ter vindo um homem a procurar o bem dos filhos de Israel.

verses.original: וָאָב֖וֹא אֶל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וָאֱהִי־ שָׁ֖ם יָמִ֥ים שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ā·ḇō·w ’el- yə·rū·šā·lim wā·’ĕ·hî- šām yā·mîm šə·lō·šāh
verses.literal: After I had arrived in Jerusalem and had been there three days
verses.literalPt: Assim, cheguei a Jerusalém e estive ali três dias.

verses.original: וָאָק֣וּם׀ לַ֗יְלָה אֲנִי֮ וַאֲנָשִׁ֣ים׀ מְעַט֮ עִמִּי֒ וְלֹא־ הִגַּ֣דְתִּי לְאָדָ֔ם מָ֗ה אֱלֹהַי֙ נֹתֵ֣ן אֶל־ לִבִּ֔י לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת לִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּבְהֵמָה֙ אֵ֣ין עִמִּ֔י כִּ֚י אִם־ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י רֹכֵ֥ב בָּֽהּ׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ā·qūm lay·lāh ’ă·nî wa·’ă·nā·šîm mə·‘aṭ ‘im·mî wə·lō- hig·gaḏ·tî lə·’ā·ḏām māh ’ĕ·lō·hay nō·ṯên ’el- lib·bî la·‘ă·śō·wṯ lî·rū·šā·lim ū·ḇə·hê·māh ’ên ‘im·mî kî ’im- hab·bə·hê·māh ’ă·šer ’ă·nî rō·ḵêḇ bāh
verses.literal: I set out at night with a few men I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem The only . . . animal . . . with me was the one on which I was riding
verses.literalPt: Levantei-me de noite, eu e uns poucos homens comigo; e não disse eu a ninguém o que o meu Deus me pôs no coração para fazer em benefício de Jerusalém. Não havia comigo animal algum senão o em que eu estava montado.

verses.original: וָאֵצְאָ֨ה בְשַֽׁעַר־ הַגַּ֜יא לַ֗יְלָה וְאֶל־ פְּנֵי֙ עֵ֣ין הַתַּנִּ֔ין וְאֶל־ שַׁ֖עַר הָאַשְׁפֹּ֑ת וָאֱהִ֨י שֹׂבֵ֜ר בְּחוֹמֹ֤ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ אֲשֶׁר־ הַמְפֹרוָצִים וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ אֻכְּל֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ê·ṣə·’āh ḇə·ša·‘ar- hag·gay lay·lāh wə·’el- pə·nê ‘ên hat·tan·nîn wə·’el- ša·‘ar hā·’aš·pōṯ wā·’ĕ·hî śō·ḇêr bə·ḥō·w·mōṯ yə·rū·šā·lim ’ă·šer- ham·p̄ō·r·wå̄·ṣīm ū·šə·ʿå̄·rɛ·hå̄ ’uk·kə·lū ḇā·’êš
verses.literal: So I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward . . . the Well of the Serpent . . . and the Dung . . . Gate and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire
verses.literalPt: Saí de noite pela Entrada do Vale, em direção à Fonte do Dragão, e até a Entrada do Esterco e contemplava os muros de Jerusalém, que estavam demolidos, e as suas portas, que tinham sido consumidas do fogo.

verses.original: וָאֶֽעֱבֹר֙ אֶל־ שַׁ֣עַר הָעַ֔יִן וְאֶל־ בְּרֵכַ֖ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵין־ מָק֥וֹם לַבְּהֵמָ֖ה לַעֲבֹ֥ר תַּחְתָּֽי׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’e·‘ĕ·ḇōr ’el- ša·‘ar hā·‘a·yin wə·’el- bə·rê·ḵaṯ ham·me·leḵ wə·’ên- mā·qō·wm lab·bə·hê·māh la·‘ă·ḇōr taḥ·tāy
verses.literal: Then I went on to the Fountain . . . Gate and the King’s Pool but there was no room for the animal under me to get through
verses.literalPt: Passei à Entrada da Fonte e à piscina do rei; porém não havia lugar por onde pudesse passar o animal em que ia montado.

verses.original: וָאֱהִ֨י עֹלֶ֤ה בַנַּ֙חַל֙ לַ֔יְלָה וָאֱהִ֥י שֹׂבֵ֖ר בַּחוֹמָ֑ה וָאָשׁ֗וּב וָאָב֛וֹא בְּשַׁ֥עַר הַגַּ֖יְא וָאָשֽׁוּב׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ĕ·hî ‘ō·leh ḇan·na·ḥal lay·lāh wā·’ĕ·hî śō·ḇêr ba·ḥō·w·māh wā·’ā·šūḇ wā·’ā·ḇō·w bə·ša·‘ar hag·gay wā·’ā·šūḇ
verses.literal: so I went up the valley by night and inspected the wall Then I headed back and reentered . . . through the Valley Gate
verses.literalPt: Subi de noite pela torrente; contemplei os muros, e, voltando, entrei pela Entrada do Vale, e assim voltei.

verses.original: וְהַסְּגָנִ֗ים לֹ֤א יָדְעוּ֙ אָ֣נָה הָלַ֔כְתִּי וּמָ֖ה אֲנִ֣י עֹשֶׂ֑ה וְלַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְלַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים וְלַחֹרִ֣ים וְלַסְּגָנִ֗ים וּלְיֶ֙תֶר֙ עֹשֵׂ֣ה הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה עַד־ כֵּ֖ן לֹ֥א הִגַּֽדְתִּי׃
verses.transliteration: wə·has·sə·ḡā·nîm lō yā·ḏə·‘ū ’ā·nāh hā·laḵ·tî ū·māh ’ă·nî ‘ō·śeh wə·lay·yə·hū·ḏîm wə·lak·kō·hă·nîm wə·la·ḥō·rîm wə·las·sə·ḡā·nîm ū·lə·ye·ṯer ‘ō·śêh ham·mə·lā·ḵāh ‘aḏ- kên lō hig·gaḏ·tî
verses.literal: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing for I had not yet . . . told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers
verses.literalPt: Os magistrados não sabiam aonde eu fui, nem o que eu fiz; nem ainda o tinha eu dito aos judeus, nem aos sacerdotes, nem aos nobres, nem aos magistrados, nem aos mais que faziam a obra.

verses.original: וָאוֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם אַתֶּ֤ם רֹאִים֙ הָרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲנַ֣חְנוּ בָ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ חֲרֵבָ֔ה וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ נִצְּת֣וּ בָאֵ֑שׁ לְכ֗וּ וְנִבְנֶה֙ אֶת־ חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְלֹא־ נִהְיֶ֥ה ע֖וֹד חֶרְפָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ō·w·mar ’ă·lê·hem ’at·tem rō·’îm hā·rā·‘āh ’ă·šer ’ă·naḥ·nū ḇāh ’ă·šer yə·rū·šā·lim ḥă·rê·ḇāh ū·šə·‘ā·re·hā niṣ·ṣə·ṯū ḇā·’êš lə·ḵū wə·niḇ·neh ’eṯ- ḥō·w·maṯ yə·rū·šā·lim wə·lō- nih·yeh ‘ō·wḏ ḥer·pāh
verses.literal: Then I said to them You see the trouble we are in Jerusalem lies in ruins and its gates have been burned down . . . Come let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem so that we will no longer be a disgrace
verses.literalPt: Eu lhes disse: Vós vedes o triste estado em que nos achamos, como Jerusalém está deserta, e as suas portas consumidas do fogo; vinde, e reedifiquemos o muro de Jerusalém, para que não sejamos mais opróbrio.

verses.original: וָאַגִּ֨יד לָהֶ֜ם אֶת־ יַ֣ד אֱלֹהַ֗י אֲשֶׁר־ הִיא֙ טוֹבָ֣ה עָלַ֔י וְאַף־ דִּבְרֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־ לִ֑י וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֔ינוּ וַיְחַזְּק֥וּ יְדֵיהֶ֖ם לַטּוֹבָֽה׃פ
verses.transliteration: wā·’ag·gîḏ lā·hem ’eṯ- yaḏ ’ĕ·lō·hay ’ă·šer- hî ṭō·w·ḇāh ‘ā·lay wə·’ap̄- diḇ·rê ham·me·leḵ ’ă·šer ’ā·mar- lî way·yō·mə·rū nā·qūm ū·ḇā·nî·nū way·ḥaz·zə·qū yə·ḏê·hem laṭ·ṭō·w·ḇāh
verses.literal: I also told them about . . . the gracious hand of my God upon me and . . . what the king had said to me Let us start rebuilding they replied and they set their hands to this good work
verses.literalPt: Referi-lhes como a mão do meu Deus me fora favorável e as palavras que o rei me tinha falado. Eles disseram: Levantemo-nos e edifiquemos. Fortaleceram as suas mãos para a boa obra.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַע֩ סַנְבַלַּ֨ט הַחֹרֹנִ֜י וְטֹבִיָּ֣ה׀ הָעֶ֣בֶד הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֗י וְגֶ֙שֶׁם֙ הָֽעַרְבִ֔י וַיַּלְעִ֣גוּ לָ֔נוּ וַיִּבְז֖וּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ מָֽה־ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים הַעַ֥ל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אַתֶּ֥ם מֹרְדִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·ma‘ san·ḇal·laṭ ha·ḥō·rō·nî wə·ṭō·ḇî·yāh hā·‘e·ḇeḏ hā·‘am·mō·w·nî wə·ḡe·šem hā·‘ar·ḇî way·yal·‘i·ḡū lā·nū way·yiḇ·zū ‘ā·lê·nū way·yō·mə·rū māh- had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh ’ă·šer ’at·tem ‘ō·śîm ha·‘al ham·me·leḵ ’at·tem mō·rə·ḏîm
verses.literal: But when Sanballat the Horonite Tobiah the Ammonite official and Geshem the Arab heard about this they mocked us and ridiculed us saying What . . . is this you are doing Are you rebelling against the king
verses.literalPt: Mas, quando Sambalá, horonita, e o servo Tobias, amonita, e Gesém, árabe, o souberam, zombaram de nós, desprezaram-nos e disseram: Que é isto que vós fazeis? Quereis rebelar-vos contra o rei?

verses.original: וָאָשִׁ֨יב אוֹתָ֜ם דָּבָ֗ר וָאוֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם ה֚וּא יַצְלִ֣יחַֽ לָ֔נוּ וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֑ינוּ וְלָכֶ֗ם אֵֽין־ חֵ֧לֶק וּצְדָקָ֛ה וְזִכָּר֖וֹן בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: wā·’ā·šîḇ ’ō·w·ṯām dā·ḇār wā·’ō·w·mar lā·hem ’ĕ·lō·hê haš·šā·ma·yim hū yaṣ·lî·aḥ lā·nū wa·’ă·naḥ·nū ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw nā·qūm ū·ḇā·nî·nū wə·lā·ḵem ’ên- ḥê·leq ū·ṣə·ḏā·qāh wə·zik·kā·rō·wn bî·rū·šā·lim
verses.literal: So I answered them and said The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success We His servants will start rebuilding but you have no portion right or claim in Jerusalem
verses.literalPt: Respondi-lhes: O Deus do céu é quem nos fará bem sucedidos; portanto, nós, seus servos, nos levantaremos e reedificaremos; mas vós não tendes parte, nem direito, nem memorial em Jerusalém.
